title: As a developer, I can search and browse a large catalog of MCP servers and tools by capability before wiring anything into my agent
As an AI agent, I can query the platform's registry or catalog through a documented API to discover servers and tools programmatically
As a developer, I can inspect a listed server's tools, input schemas, transport, and hosting attributes before connecting to it
As a developer, I can exercise an MCP server's tools from a browser-based inspector or playground before integrating it
As a developer, I can point my MCP-compatible client at a hosted remote server URL and reach downstream tools without deploying any infrastructure
As a developer, I can reach a deep catalog of third-party apps and APIs (hundreds to thousands of integrations) through the platform
As a developer, I can publish my own MCP server on the platform for distribution, discovery, and installation by others
As a developer, I can turn an existing API definition (OpenAPI) or custom code into a hosted MCP server without writing protocol plumbing
As a developer, I can subscribe my agent to events from connected downstream apps (triggers/webhooks) instead of polling them
As a developer, I can let the platform run OAuth flows for downstream tools and vault the resulting credentials encrypted, with automatic token refresh
As a platform-engineer, I can maintain separate connected accounts and scoped tokens per end user of my product, so each user's agent acts only on that user's credentials
As a platform-engineer, I can white-label the authorization flow with my own branding and my own OAuth app credentials
As a platform-engineer, I can restrict which servers and individual tools an agent may call through allowlists or per-tool access control
As a platform-engineer, I can see a log of every tool call that passed through the platform, with enough detail to audit or replay what an agent did
As a platform-engineer, I can rely on the platform scanning or inspecting listed servers for malicious or vulnerable behavior before my agents use them
As a developer, I can compare servers using published quality signals — usage counts, health or liveness checks, scores, or verification badges
As an AI agent, I can search and load tools at runtime through meta-tools instead of having thousands of tool definitions stuffed into my context
As a developer, I can plug the platform's tools into major agent frameworks and SDKs (Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI or Anthropic SDKs) with documented adapters
As a developer, I can drive the publish-and-deploy workflow from an official CLI — authenticate, stage or build a server, push it, and install it into agents
As a platform-engineer, I can see usage analytics for the servers and tools my org consumes or publishes — call volumes, users, errors, and cost
As a developer, I can bridge a locally running MCP server into the platform as a managed remote connection without deploying it
As a developer, I can see transparent pricing per tool call or connection plus documented rate limits before committing to the platform
As a developer, I can prototype my agent's tool connections on a meaningful free tier before paying anything
